side_a: CC 3.1.3.3: "**`federation` for Commons and `public` content**. The substrate refuses a report whose scope is not its content's."
side_b: CC 5.2: "the only plaintext bodies are those of authorized infrastructure communities and public rooms, which"
note: CC 5.2 and CC 1.13.3.4 put an authorized infrastructure community's holding claims at federation scope with the public room's; CC 3.1.3.3 rule (1) names only Commons and public content for federation and refuses any other report whose scope is not its content's (`community`). A reader of rule (1) refuses the infrastructure community's federation-scope custody report that a reader of CC 5.2 emits. CC 4.4.3.2.1 (plaintext by the record) supports CC 5.2.

side_a: CC 6.1.5.3: "has an allow list of only the cohorts it was set up to serve"
side_b: CC 3.3.7: "receives **no** `self` content beyond the two arms below, and **no** `family` content unless the list names it"
note: A server-class node whose grant carries no `cohorts` member: CC 6.1.5.3 gives it only the cohorts it was set up to serve; the class default of CC 3.3.7 (and the later sentence of CC 6.1.5.3) withholds only self and family, so every community and affiliation of its owner replicates onto it. The two give different holdings for the owner's other communities. Near C381 (which asks about agents), not the same point.

side_a: CC 3.1.3.1: "**Projection ceiling: `Cohort` at every commons tier, with no `authority` branch (normative — not a default).**"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json session:{kind} placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text forbids a session claim above the cohort (an attendance map of a person's devices); the model cell lets the signer place it in the commons, where the replication cell serves it to everyone. The cell is marked a gap; the text has the value.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: "the audience is the cell (for an agent, the steward's cohort and the WA it routes to), never a federation broadcast"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json deferral:request placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text bounds a deferral request to the deferring party's cell; the model cell admits it at commons placement with audience everyone, and the CC 8.10 card shows attest widening by scope. Text has the value; the data cell is a gap.

side_a: CC 3.1.4: "A federation-scope row whose attester and subject are one **rendezvous key**"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json rendezvous:route placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text fixes the route row at federation scope with reach everyone; the model cell leaves placement to the signer. A route placed narrower reaches no sender, so a careful reader resolves it the text's way.

side_a: CC 3.2: "there is no member-level listing, and a roster is never enumerable outside its cohort, a public room's included"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json membership:{stage} replication.audience note: "may_receive_group_plane (public group: everyone; private: members' nodes, live invitees, named member); proposal: addressee (invitee)"
note: CC 3.2 and the CC 5.2 audience table (public room: an outsider learns the listing, the holding claims and the content, "never the roster") keep a public room's membership rows inside its roster; the model cell serves a public group's membership rows to everyone, which makes the roster enumerable by any node.

side_a: CC 5.4.6: "A node offers an `identity:occurrence:v1` row to a peer only when it would also relay the row's attester key to that peer"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json identity:occurrence replication.audience note: "key-plane reach (Plane::KeyRecord cells; the carrier: everyone)"
note: CC 5.4.6 withholds an occurrence whose attester's owner-binding is not announced, and holds an unannounced identity's occurrence with the owner's nodes and the contact alone; the model cell gives the family one audience, everyone. A kernel reading the cell serves an unannounced person's occurrence to strangers.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — addressed:** a member of the room; reach is the named tally member only"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json census:member:share replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Same fault as C383 on the sibling family: the text holds a member's community cell with its author and the one tally member it is addressed to; the model cell keeps the default audience (the whole cohort plus subjects) under an `addressed` placement.

side_a: CC 6.1.9: "is held by the author's node and the recipient's node and by no other"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json census:share:{class} replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Still present: the census:share:{class} replication cell still carries the default audience, not the addressee.

side_a: CC 4.5.5: "A duty-holder's record MAY withhold the reporter's identity and the report's content from the person named"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json moderation:{allegation_type} replication.audience: "cohort_plus_subjects(full) (refers-to: attested, subjects, for_key_id)"
note: Still present: the moderation cell still serves the full row to the subject; the text lets the record reach the person named as existence, kind, consequence and answerer only.

side_a: CC 1.13.3.1: "An observer learns that a group exists, roughly how big it is, and when its membership churns."
side_b: CC 2.1: "So `family_id` is consulted in-substrate and never on the wire to non-members."
note: Still present (resolution proposed, not applied): CC 1.13.3.1 concedes that an observer sees a family's existence, size and churn; CC 2.1 and the CC 5.2 table (an outsider learns nothing, "not even that the content exists", and nothing of the roster) deny it unless the observer is inside the cohort.

side_a: CC 6.1.1: "`cohort_scope: family | community` content MAY be witnessed **only at the opaque `content_id`/manifest-digest grain**"
side_b: CC 5.2: "the only attestations that refer to them are scoped to the cohort and never federate beyond it"
note: CC 6.1.1 does not state the audience of a wholeness witness whose leaves include family content, and WW-4 publishes a `leaf_count`; CC 5.2 lets no row that refers to family bytes leave the cohort. A careful reader places such a witness at the family's scope, which CC 6.1.1 should say.

side_a: CC 3.1.4: "each period's row `supersedes` the previous one in the same lineage"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json rendezvous:route supersede roles: "author"
note: CC 3.1.4 gives each period a fresh rendezvous key that is attester and subject of its row, so the row that supersedes last period's is signed by a different key; the transition (and the CC 2.4.1 gloss, "by the same attester") lets only the prior row's author supersede. A kernel run from the data refuses every period's successor. The supersedes link also ties one period's key to the next, which the fresh key was to prevent.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "a Goal is amended by `supersedes`, retired by `withdraws`, and disowned by `recants`"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json goal:{scale} verbs: ["attest", "replace", "withdraw"]
note: The text gives a Goal's declarer `recants`; the model's verb cell (source cc-table) and the transitions omit it, though the cell's own code reading records "+recant". A door built from the data refuses the recant the text admits. approach:{goal_id} carries recant; goal does not.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: "(`supersedes` to revise, `withdraws` to satisfy/close, `recants` if misstated)"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json need:{domain}:{kind} verbs: ["attest", "replace", "withdraw"]
note: Same fault as goal:{scale}: the text gives a need row `recants`, the verb cell and transitions have attest, supersede and withdraw only.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.7: "its `supersedes`, `withdraws` and `recants` stand only when they too are cosigned under the same protocol"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json goal:{scale} supersede: roles "author", policy "selfAct"
note: For a Goal a group declared, the text requires the amendment, retirement and disowning to be cosigned under the group's protocol; the model has cosign_rule none and one-signer supersede and withdraw, so one member who signed first amends or retires the group's Goal alone. The same holds for approach, method and progress_measure rows a group declares.

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "`census_composite_duplicate_period` (a second composite for the class and period, from any seat)"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json census:composite:{class}: verbs attest, withdraw, supersede; supersede roles "author"
note: The text allows one composite per class and period and refuses a second from any seat; the transitions and the CC 8.10 card give the signing seat a supersede (and a withdraw), which is a second composite for the same class and period. census:partial:{class} carries the same supersede against "one per (seat, class, period)".

side_a: CC 3.1.3: "**Yes — the accord holders, cosigned at the charter's M**; never a single holder, never the node itself"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json transport:canonical_rebind supersede: roles "author", policy "selfAct"
note: The attest transition now carries the cosigned accord policy (C369, C374 fixed there), but the supersede transition beside it is still one-signer: the holder who authored a re-bind replaces it alone, which is a re-bind by a single holder. The CC 8.10 card shows the same line.

side_a: CC 3.3.4: "A `family` Contribution that supersedes the current one may change metadata or drop members and never adds one."
side_b: CC 4.4.3.4.2: "A membership change is never a single-signer `supersedes` Contribution, which a rule-1 or rule-2 `withdraws` could retire without the quorum."
note: CC 3.3.4 lets a superseding family Contribution drop members, and a `supersedes` is its attester's act (CC 2.4.1); the same item then says removal is a cosigned `membership:removal` or a resignation, and CC 4.4.3.4.2 and CC 4.4.3.2.3 say no membership change is a `supersedes`. A reader of the first sentence lets one signer remove a member. The rest of the document supports CC 4.4.3.4.2; the model has "typed record supersede only".

side_a: CC 6.1.1: "MUST NOT replace `monotonic_quorum` / `revision` anti-rollback for `revocation` / `partner_record` / `org_membership`"
side_b: CC 5.3.2.3: "**`lww_skew_bounded` + `withdrawal_forward_only`**"
note: CC 6.1.1 names org_membership (and partner_record) as merged by monotonic_quorum with revision anti-rollback; CC 5.3.2.3, the home of merge policy, gives organization and org_membership latest-wins with forward-only withdrawal and has no partner_record row; CC 3.3.9 calls all three retired kinds. The hand-off in CC 6.1.1 is to CC 5.3.2.3 either way, so the outcome is that section's.

side_a: CC 2.4.1.2.1: "`rotation_chain` is supersession lineage, not onward transfer."
side_b: CC 5.1: "an informative trail of the prior `key_grant_id`s; no row supersedes or removes a wrap"
note: One member, two descriptions: a supersession lineage in CC 2.4.1.2.1, and in CC 5.1 and CC 3.3.2 a trail under which no wrap supersedes another ("A wrap once admitted is never removed by a later one"). A reader of CC 2.4.1.2.1 alone could retire the earlier wrap.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.5.3: ".latest_by(asserted_at)   # signed by the user; subject_key_id = the agent occurrence"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "so revoking the newest grant never resurrects an older one"
note: ratified_pair drops withdrawn rows and then takes the latest remaining grant, so withdrawing the newest partnership grant brings back an older one under the same pair id; the boundary fold of CC 3.3.1 and CC 4.4.3.5.5 puts every earlier grant out. CC 3.3.1 states the boundary for community_trust and consent:state only, so the partnership leaves are not strictly covered.

side_a: CC 2.4.1: "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: data manifests/transitions.json: "verb": "supersede"
note: Still present: the CC 2.4.1 table cell still says "by the same attester" while Part 3 has other-signer supersession (the cosigned re-bind that supersedes a bundle-seeded binding, the accord recovery signed under the recovery key, the new guardian).

side_a: CC 2.4.1: "This attestation row replaces a prior one by the same attester"
side_b: CC 3.2: "a new guardian's `delegates_to` carried as a `supersedes` ([CC 2.4.1.1](part_2_the_grammar.md)) replaces the prior binding"
note: Known and open with the steward: whether a new guardian displaces the old by their own row. Reported because this reading reaches it independently.

side_a: CC 3.1.2.1: "A rebuild is a `supersedes` on the earlier Contribution"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json provenance:build_manifest:{target} verbs: ["attest", "withdraw"]
note: Still present: the provenance families have no supersede transition and no replace verb.

side_a: CC 4.3: "on window expiry it re-routes to the live quorum"
side_b: CC 4.3: "re-routes under rule 1 to the party's other live seats and, with none, to the conferrer"
note: Who answers a deferral whose Wise Authority has lapsed: rule 1 and the `deferral:request` row of CC 3.1.9.3 send it to "the live quorum", a body; the seat rule sends it to the other seats this party conferred and then to the conferrer (for an agent, its steward), and CC 4.3 says there is no roster of Wise Authorities. A reader of rule 1 alone routes an agent's deferral to a board the steward never seated. The seat rule is the later and more specific text.

side_a: CC 1.13.2: "`consent:partnered` is theirs to revoke ([CC 3.3.1](part_3_the_namespace.md))"
side_b: CC 3.3.1: "A leaf with no named emitter class is unregistered, and a consumer MUST reject it"
note: CC 1.13.2, CC 4.4.3.4.3 (the agency row), CC 2.1, CC 4.5.1.1 and CC 5.3.2.2 name a dimension `consent:partnered` or `consent:partnered:{user_key}` (the agent-side stance). The closed leaf set of CC 3.3.1 has no `partnered` leaf: the pair is `consent:partnership_grant` and `consent:partnership_accept`, and `partnered` is a kind of `consent:stream`. A node following CC 5.3.2.2 emits a row a node following CC 3.3.1 rejects; and what a person revokes to end an agent's partnership is named differently in the two.

side_a: CC 4.4.3.4.3: "The agent occurrence's withdrawal ends the binding and enters the objection path of the retirement machine"
side_b: CC 4.5.1: "**agent:** none while held — this cell is stated, not hidden"
note: CC 4.4.3.4.3 gives the agent occurrence a withdrawal that "ends the binding" and calls it "leaving"; the register's exit cell and CC 1.13.2 ("no release from stewardship") give a held agent no exit. They agree only if "the binding" is the data partnership and not the stewardship, which CC 4.4.3.4.3 does not say (its previous sentence says the accept half is signed "under the owner-binding").

side_a: CC 7.3.4: "a CIRIS agent's hold over a made thing does not loosen as that thing's capacity grows"
side_b: CC 1.13.2: "A key that cannot accept for itself is held by an accountable human who answers for it"
note: CC 7.3.4 writes the hold as a CIRIS agent's over a made thing; everywhere else the holder is an accountable human and the agent is what is held. Read literally CC 7.3.4 lets an agent be a steward. The sentence most likely means the hold over a CIRIS agent.

side_a: CC 1.16.5: "Appointment, rotation, recusal, and appeals are external to this system’s control and follow explicit anti-capture rules."
side_b: CC 4.3: "A seat over one party's deferrals is conferred by that party in a signed row and by nobody else"
note: Still present: CC 1.16.5 is unchanged, and the opening of CC 4.3 restates it ("external to this system's control") three paragraphs above the seat rule. CC 1.16.4 still transmits to "the designated Wise Authorities".

side_a: CC 3.3.13: "User-private; always `cohort_scope: self`; promotable via [CC 4.4.3.3.1](part_4_composition_governance.md)"
side_b: CC 4.4.3.3.1: "optionally morph `sub_kind`"
note: CC 3.3.13 holds a `local_data` row at self always; CC 4.4.3.3.1 makes the change of sub_kind on promotion optional, so a widened row may still be `local_data` at community or federation scope. A door that enforced "always self" would refuse the promotion CC 4.4.3.3 describes unless the sub_kind changes.

side_a: CC 3.1.5.5: "Emitted at `federation` scope by a key holding `infra:attest`"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json evidence:{suite}:{kind}:{cell}:{prefix} placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: The text fixes an evidence row at federation scope (its blob is a Commons blob); the model cell leaves placement to the signer and is marked a gap. The text has the value.

side_a: CC 3.4.5.1: "`admission` (admin key ids), `transport` (bootstrap peers, peer sideband) — MUST be emitted at `self`"
side_b: data manifests/family_model.json config:{scope} placement: "any of {self_collective, targeted_family, targeted_room, commons}, signer-chosen (GAP: no per-family constraint)"
note: CC 3.4.5.1 leaves config placement per row but pins two leaves to self by MUST; the model has one cell for the family with no per-leaf arm, so the data cannot refuse a `config:admission` row at a wider scope. Whether the MUST is a door or an emitter duty the text does not say.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: "MUST surface it as a conformance failure (`namespace_family_unregistered`), never admit-and-wait"
side_b: CC 3.1.7: "so a consumer resolving its authority falls through to the producer-steward default"
note: Known and open with the steward: whether a row of an unregistered family is refused or admitted under the producer-steward default. Reported because this reading reaches it independently; the "Where the fallback remains" sentence narrows the default to open vocabulary and does not say what a receiving node does.

side_a: CC 3.1.7: "A substrate observing emission on a family with no registry row (provisional or ratified) MUST surface it as a conformance failure"
side_b: CC 3.1.7: "The prefix is the legitimate unregistered range whose absence is what mints `X-`-convention squatting"
note: R2(b) makes every emission on a family with no registry row a conformance failure; the private-use paragraph makes `x_private:{anything}` a legitimate unregistered range, refused only at federation tier. R2(b) states no exception for it. A careful reader exempts the prefix carried in `_meta.private_use_prefix`.

side_a: CC 3.1.9.3: "The registry owner is CIRISNodeCore; the wire shape of the request is the substrate's. Open emitter."
side_b: data manifests/namespace_registry.json deferral:request: "reserved": true, reserved_rule cc_ref "CC 3.1.9.4"
note: The catalogue row calls deferral:request an open emitter; the registry marks it reserved, with a rule (the deferring party's own key) that reserves nothing, and cites CC 3.1.9.4 for a row that sits in CC 3.1.9.3.

side_a: CC 3.2: "a canonical holds the listing row and nothing else unless it joins"
side_b: CC 3.1.3.3: "At federation scope that audience is everyone, and the `here` rows **are** the holder directory a consumer reads to find holders"
note: A public room's custody reports sit at federation scope (CC 4.4.3.2.1), whose audience is every node and which serve seats carry among themselves by anti-entropy (CC 6.1.5.3); CC 3.2 says a canonical holds the room's listing and nothing else. A careful reader takes "nothing else" to mean none of the content.

side_a: CC 3.2: "**byte-level confidentiality to members + provenance-visible discovery**"
side_b: CC 3.2: "communities keep their bytes, their roster and their holders from outsiders too"
note: The phrase C274 settled against CC 5.2 still stands in the DEK-cascade paragraph of CC 3.2, eighty lines below the sentence of the same section that keeps a community's holders and roster from outsiders and makes only a public room discoverable.
